children: Broadcom, a semiconductor and infrastructure-software supplier
, launched Arcot Scam Defense on Wednesday, targeting payment scams that survive successful customer authentication. Shares stood at $322.55 at 11.35am EST on Thursday, down approximately 4.51%

The pitch is straightforward: catch suspicious payments even after customers clear security checks. Broadcom's pilot findings estimated that reviewing the riskiest 1% of successful authentication challenges at one major issuer could have prevented $4 million in fraud over one month. The projected tradeoff was a 0.38-percentage-point reduction in authentication success. That is a promising result, but it remains an estimate from one issuer.

The valuation chart puts shares 25.42% below the $432.51 GF Value estimate, suggesting potential upside if the business delivers. That discount alone does not establish a bargain. Broadcom's announcement provided neither product pricing nor a revenue forecast. The next test is commercial: how many issuers adopt the feature, how much payment volume it covers and what customers will pay.

title: Broadcom Stocks Dip 4.5% After New AI Fraud Defense Launch
